races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap

runners_data.name: Bintkend
runners_data.note: Prominent style gives her tactical advantage over deeper closers in this pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and well-bred filly; open to significant improvement on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed filly; did not live up to pedigree in her three qualifying races but kept on for third behind a fairly useful filly in a Wolverhampton maiden (9.4f, AW) in February and could have significant improvement to come in handicaps.

runners_data.name: A Major Payne
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage but 5lb penalty offset by Wednesday's confidence-boosting win
runners_data.comment: Carries 5lb penalty for Wednesday's Nottingham win but ought to be in the shake-up again
runners_data.spotlight: Placed three consecutive times before leading close home to open account at Nottingham (1m2f, good; front pair clear) on Wednesday, carries 5lb penalty here but should be fine on the forecast slower ground; ought to be right in the thick of things again.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Front-running style perfectly suited to uncontested lead scenario on 19-day break
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; ran well when placed behind King's Hand over C&D on recent stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who gave good account when placed behind King's Hand over C&D (good) on last month's stable debut; that run came after a layoff and he remains on a good mark; handles good to soft (unraced on anything slower); no surprise if he makes a bold bid.

runners_data.name: King's Hand
runners_data.note: Hold-up tactics problematic when conceding early ground to uncontested pace setter
runners_data.comment: Did well to win over C&D last month, after a slow start, but is a bit of a character
runners_data.spotlight: Signed off for Sir Mark Prescott with 1m2f AW win here in January and has performed well on all four starts for new stable, most notably when recovering from a slow start to win over C&D (1m2f, good) last month; still unexposed on turf but he often races too freely and is a bit of a character.

runners_data.name: Kokanee
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs pace collapse to be effective from deep position
runners_data.comment: Not making any progress but went close over 1m two starts ago and this trip also suits
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make any significant further progress since winning handicap debut at Beverley (1m2f, good) in spring 2025 but went close at Pontefract (1m, good to soft) two starts ago and should cope if the ground remains soft.

runners_data.name: Kaaranah
runners_data.note: Cheekpieces boost not enough to overcome hold-up disadvantage in this tactical setup
runners_data.spotlight: Seemingly boosted by cheekpieces when winning twice at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in April and endured a wide trip before keeping on steadily for sixth at Kempton (1m, AW; no headgear, as today) last month; versatile ground-wise on turf; can't be ignored.

runners_data.name: Birthday Angel
runners_data.note: 233-day absence and hold-up style creates double disadvantage against uncontested leader
runners_data.comment: In good form on Flat/over hurdles in the autumn but has fitness to prove after break
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on the Flat at Brighton (1m2f, good to soft) in October and added two hurdle wins to his tally the following month; probably still on a workable Flat mark and seems versatile regarding ground but has fitness to prove after 172-day absence.

races.paceDynamic: Bobacious will set the pace as the sole confirmed front-runner with sustainable early gallop over this 1m2f trip on soft ground. The lack of pace pressure means he can dictate fractions and potentially steal a march on the field. With most rivals adopting hold-up tactics (A Major Payne, King's Hand, Kokanee, Kaaranah, Birthday Angel), they'll need to overcome the tactical disadvantage of conceding lengths early. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and pace-setters who can exploit the uncontested lead scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Setter Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious gets uncontested fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: His front-running style becomes a significant weapon when unopposed early, allowing him to build an unassailable lead. The hold-up brigade face an impossible task catching a horse who's controlled the tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses can close the gap despite conceding early ground
scenarios.body: A Major Payne and King's Hand have the class to overcome tactical disadvantage if Bobacious weakens in the final furlong. Their recent form edge and superior ratings could prevail in a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Bintkend settles handily behind Bobacious and times her challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: Racing closer to the pace gives her the ideal position to strike when the leader tires. Her prominent style suits this tactical scenario better than the deep closers who'll have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious stops completely and allows the entire field back into contention
scenarios.body: A blanket finish develops where class tells and the highest-rated horses prevail despite poor positioning. King's Hand and A Major Payne's superior ability shines through in a scrambled finale.

watchPoints.text: Bobacious getting uncontested fractions early - if unopposed he becomes very hard to peg back
A Major Payne and King's Hand struggling to get into contention turning for home from hold-up positions
Bintkend's position after two furlongs - needs to track Bobacious closely to have any chance
How quickly the hold-up horses can close the gap in the straight after conceding early ground
Whether Bobacious shows any signs of stopping in the final furlong after controlling the pace

races.name: Buy A Share At daretodreamracing.co.uk Handicap

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who faded late at Windsor last time but soft ground should suit better than good to firm conditions.
runners_data.comment: Competitive off his mark but wouldn't be sure to benefit from tthis step back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up on reappearance when third of ten over 1m at Windsor (good to firm) a fortnight ago, although he faded inside the final furlong and this sometimes keen goer wouldn't be sure to benefit from this slightly longer distance.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making turf debut who caught the eye when denied clear runs at Haydock, should get easier time here.
runners_data.comment: Pulls hard but an eyecatcher on recent handicap and turf debut; gets the vote
runners_data.spotlight: Caught the eye (repeatedly denied a clear run) when keeping on late for fourth of 11 on 1m Haydock handicap and turf debut (good to soft) 15 days ago; possibly not entirely straightforward (has taken a keen hold on most starts) but it's likely he has the ability to win off this mark.

runners_data.name: Rajendra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 100-day break for in-form David Simcock yard, appeals as potential improver fresh.
runners_data.comment: Has hinted at ability in his qualifying runs and appeals as a likely improver in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Tough to argue his opening mark is generous on bare form but he's more than hinted at ability and appeals as a potential improver back from a 100-day break.

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who broke maiden at 12th attempt last week but faces 6lb penalty for that Nottingham success.
runners_data.comment: Not obviously well treated under a 6lb penalty for last weekend's breakthrough win
runners_data.spotlight: Came good at the 12th time of asking when seeing off six rivals at Nottingham (extended 1m, good) last Sunday; not obviously well treated under a 6lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has placed twice in handicaps this spring but showed disappointing form on soft ground last year.
runners_data.comment: Third in both handicaps and too soon to suggest he's reached his limit
runners_data.spotlight: Third around 1m at Nottingham (good) and Yarmouth (good to firm) switched to handicaps this spring; below the level of those efforts on soft ground last year but it was his debut; has a useful pedigree and too soon to suggest he's reached his limit.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from five-month break with encouraging third at Windsor, low weight helps his chances.
runners_data.spotlight: Showed he can be competitive in handicaps at the second attempt when returning from five months off to finish third of 14 over 1m at Windsor 12 days ago; raced only on good/good to firm on turf; claims with Mason Paetel taking a handy 5lb off.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won on soft ground last autumn and returned with victory on reappearance, wide draw potential excuse.
runners_data.comment: Two 1m Bath wins, including on soft; possible excuse for lesser run last time
runners_data.spotlight: Winner over 1m at Bath on soft last autumn and returned to the same venue to double his tally on reappearance (good to firm); a wide trip provides a possible excuse for a lesser effort at Windsor since (Fans Favourite ahead of him).

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Bay is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should be allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo without pressure. The prominent runners (Daretobedifferent, Del Corso, Takeitorleaveit) will likely sit just behind but none have shown aggressive tendencies to challenge early. This sets up a moderate pace that will gradually build, with the real action coming in the final three furlongs as the hold-up horses (Royal Bodyguard, Rajendra, Fans Favourite) try to make their moves. This race shape clearly favors prominent runners who can track the leader and kick when it matters, as they'll have positional advantage without facing a searching pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Bay sets a manageable tempo and the prominent horses track him comfortably
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows Daretobedifferent and Del Corso to stay close and strike decisively when Sovereign Bay weakens, while hold-up horses struggle to make up ground. Their tactical positioning proves crucial on soft ground where acceleration is limited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Bay's stamina kicks in and he maintains his early advantage throughout
scenarios.body: His uncontested lead allows him to find a rhythm that suits his style, and when the challengers come they can't reel him in on ground that blunts their finishing kicks. Royal Bodyguard emerges best of the closers but falls short.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes slower than expected and the closing horses get ideal timing
scenarios.body: The moderate tempo allows Rajendra or Royal Bodyguard to position perfectly and unleash decisive late runs that catch the prominent horses off guard. Fresh legs prove decisive in the soft conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Bay goes too slow early and multiple horses converge simultaneously in a bunched finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early tempo creates a messy sprint where positioning and luck matter more than class, allowing an outsider like Fans Favourite to sneak through on the rails. Takeitorleaveit's wide trip becomes an advantage.

watchPoints.text: Sovereign Bay could steal this if allowed completely uncontested lead by prominent horses sitting too far back
Royal Bodyguard's stamina limitations showed at Windsor when fading late despite strong position turning for home
Daretobedifferent may struggle under 6lb penalty just six days after breaking his maiden at Nottingham
Rajendra represents David Simcock who is 0 from 9 in last 14 days but horse returns fresh after long break
Takeitorleaveit's wide draw could force him to race outside horses throughout and compromise his prominent style

runners_data.name: Cherringham

runners_data.name: Fabled Spirit

runners_data.name: Cold Fish
runners_data.comment: Promising 3rd on both runs (1m2f/1m); this could be his best trip for now; leading player
runners_data.spotlight: Third on debut at Chelmsford (1m2f, AW) last December and again showed promise when occupying the same position at Goodwood (1m, good) last month; shaped last time as though the return to 1m2f would suit; leading player.

runners_data.name: Probation
runners_data.comment: He's made the frame on both starts; open to improvement and could be in the shake-up
runners_data.spotlight: He hasn't threatened on his first two starts (9.4f/1m2f, AW/good to firm) but has shown promise and made the frame on each occasion; open to improvement and could be in the shake-up.

runners_data.name: Ataturk
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on both starts; he'll be of greater interest when stepped up in trip

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing cheekpieces for the second time after breaking her maiden just seven days ago, but her style is poorly suited to a likely uncontested pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces and reduced mark when off the mark (6f, good to firm) one week ago; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Fresh cheekpieces may have helped when she took advantage of a reduced mark to open her account at Catterick (6f, good to firm) one week ago; up 6lb but started quickly to make all that day so has to be feared with the potential to bag the favoured stands' rail if clearing Jane Of The Jungle; yet to be tested on ground worse than good but her dam recorded best effort on soft.

runners_data.name: Rosieisme Darling
runners_data.note: Prominent runner ideally positioned to track the leader, though her lack of experience on ground softer than good creates some uncertainty about her effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Best turf run when third (6f, good) 19 days ago; softer ground a query but 5f likely isn't
runners_data.spotlight: Untried on softer than good ground; three runs on turf and the best of them came last time out when third of 12 at Windsor (6f, good) 19 days ago; was mucked about that day and this dual 5f AW winner should be fine back down in trip, especially given a likely good gallop despite the small field.

runners_data.name: Jane Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who will likely get her own way in front, having shown consistent form in similar small fields and handled soft ground before.
runners_data.spotlight: Another front-runner who was involved in a blanket finish when fourth behind dead-heater My Mate Mackley at Chepstow (5f, good to soft) on her penultimate start; not so good at 6f eight days ago but a sharp break could put her in pole position to bag the rail.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Recently gelded hold-up horse whose dead-heat at Chepstow with Jane Of The Jungle gives him solid form claims, but needs pace pressure that may not materialize.
runners_data.comment: Gelded and took a step forward on h'cap debut when dead-heating latest; unexposed sprinter
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded ahead of his handicap debut and it was a good step forward when on the pace before sharing the spoils at Chepstow (5f, good to soft; Jane Of The Jungle fourth) 16 days ago; that was his first go at this trip and the handicapper could only dish out a 1lb nudge to this unexposed sprinter.

races.paceDynamic: Jane Of The Jungle will set the pace with minimal pressure in this small field, creating a sustainable tempo through the early furlongs. Rosieisme Darling may track her prominently but lacks the natural speed to apply serious pressure. The hold-up horses Zoustar Dreams and My Mate Mackley will need the pace to collapse or find gaps in the straight. This race shape clearly favors front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace without stress.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Jane Of The Jungle gets an easy lead and maintains her rhythm
scenarios.body: She dictates terms throughout and kicks clear when asked, with the soft ground suiting her recent Chepstow form. The hold-up horses struggle to make up ground against a horse who's had everything her own way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Rosieisme Darling can stay in touch and produce her Windsor form
scenarios.body: She travels smoothly behind Jane Of The Jungle before unleashing a strong finish, benefiting from the tactical advantage of sitting second. Her good ground form translates well enough to the softer conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and gaps appear in the straight
scenarios.body: Zoustar Dreams times her run perfectly from the back, taking advantage of her recent Catterick win momentum and fresh cheekpieces. The reduced pace allows her hold-up style to be effective over this minimum trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Gelding Effect Powers Through
scenarios.trigger: If My Mate Mackley shows significant improvement from his recent operation
scenarios.body: The gelding operation transforms his attitude and he produces a career-best effort, storming home from his customary hold-up position. His dead-heat at Chepstow proves he has the ability when things click.

watchPoints.text: Jane Of The Jungle getting a soft lead through the first two furlongs will make her very difficult to peg back in this small field
Rosieisme Darling's ground handling on her first try beyond good conditions could determine her chances of tracking the leader effectively

My Mate Mackley showing early enthusiasm would suggest the gelding operation has had the desired attitude adjustment

races.paceDynamic: Princess Maitha and Show Me Gold will lead early with Drymee and Ernie McCrew tracking close behind in the prominent positions. The soft ground will slow the early fractions making it easier for the leaders to maintain their positions through the middle stages of this 7½f contest. With limited early pace pressure and 13 runners creating cover, the race sets up perfectly for horses that can sit handy and kick when it matters. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and patient hold-up horses who can finish, while pure front-runners may struggle to sustain their effort on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is steady and the field stays bunched through halfway
scenarios.body: Princess Maitha and Show Me Gold can dictate terms from their forward positions and prove too strong in the finish. The testing ground saps the finishing kick from hold-up horses who get too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders go too fast trying to steal the race
scenarios.body: The soft ground catches up with the pace-setters in the final furlong allowing patient hold-up types to sweep past. Late runners find clear racing room with tired horses ahead dropping back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Nothing But Love or Call Alert show significant improvement from their connections
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced horses benefit from race fitness work at home and catch the more exposed runners napping. Fresh legs prove decisive against horses showing their limitations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Princess Maitha and Show Me Gold both miss the break or get shuffled back
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish from the 3f pole with no sustained pace early. This turns into a cavalry charge where any horse can win if they get a clear run.

watchPoints.text: Princess Maitha could be rusty after 318 days off despite her class advantage
Nothing But Love and Call Alert are complete unknowns who could surprise if professionally handled
Show Me Gold's fitness from recent AW runs gives her an edge over long-absent rivals
The soft ground will punish any horse that gets too far back early in this big field
Dovecote's gelding operation and stable switch could unlock improvement from promising pedigree

races.paceDynamic: Queue Dos will take this field along from the front with Monsieur Kodi and Raffles Angel likely to sit prominent in the early exchanges. With just one confirmed front-runner, Queue Dos can dictate a measured gallop that won't stretch the field early doors. The pace will be sustainable rather than punishing, allowing the hold-up horses to get competitive positions without being strung out. This tactical setup clearly favours the prominent racers and those with early pace, as they can position close to Queue Dos without pressure and have first run when the race develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Queue Dos leads uncontested and sets an even tempo throughout
scenarios.body: The measured pace allows prominent racers to travel smoothly and strike first when the sprint develops. Hold-up horses struggle to make up ground against those already well-positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Queue Dos finds another gear in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: The leader exploits the honest pace by quickening when others expect more of the same gallop. Late closers are caught flat-footed by the change of tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too slow and bunches the field
scenarios.body: A strongly-run finish develops with hold-up horses getting the fast finish they need. The prominent horses are vulnerable to being swamped late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favors Speed
scenarios.trigger: If Queue Dos faces unexpected early pressure from multiple sources
scenarios.body: The pace becomes unsustainably strong, setting up a sprint finish that suits fresh closers. Early leaders pay the price for the fast gallop.

watchPoints.text: Queue Dos breaking smartly to establish early lead position as this will dictate the entire pace scenario
Monsieur Kodi and Raffles Angel tracking the leader closely in the opening two furlongs to confirm prominent scenario
Pixie Diva getting a smooth passage through the field in the final quarter-mile given her hold-up requirements
Any early pressure on Queue Dos from unexpected sources which would completely change the pace dynamic
Charlie Mason and Hierarchy positioning in midfield rather than being held up, suggesting connections expect honest pace

races.paceDynamic: Zambezi Diamond will lead this field from the start, with Beau Jardine, Kessaar Power and Daddy Chill settling in behind to track the pace. The sole front-runner should get an easy lead and control the tempo through the early stages, but Zambezi Diamond has a clear pattern of fading in the finish. This sets up perfectly for hold-up horses who can stay out of trouble early and finish strongly. The race shape strongly favours closers who can come from off the pace in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Diamond sets steady fractions and predictably weakens in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks, with Court Of Session and No Gain best positioned to capitalize. Both have shown strong closing ability and benefit from this uncontested pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Beau Jardine or Kessaar Power can track the leader without being forced wide or into traffic
scenarios.body: The horses sitting just off the pace avoid the leader's fade while getting first run on the hold-up brigade. Kessaar Power's rail draw becomes crucial in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Diamond goes off too fast or multiple horses pressure the leader early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 3f pole, suiting horses with natural speed who don't need time to wind up. This chaotic pace benefits those with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Diamond finds improvement and the closers leave their run too late
scenarios.body: The front-runner finally breaks his pattern of fading, holding off a late charge that comes just too late. This requires perfect judgment from Thomas Greatrex.

watchPoints.text: Zambezi Diamond's early fractions will dictate the entire race outcome - too fast kills his chances, too slow helps the closers even more
Kessaar Power returning after 105 days off but his rail draw could be decisive if he's ready to go
Court Of Session backing up quickly from Wednesday's Nottingham win, watch for any signs of that effort telling
Daddy Chill's headstrong tendencies under the 7lb claimer could create early pace pressure on Zambezi Diamond
No Gain in cheekpieces again after his course success, watch Pat Cosgrave for timing of his move from the back
